instruction: Predict and write the console output order of this JavaScript code, then give the code with numbered outputs: console.log("A"); setTimeout(() => console.log("B"), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("C")); console.log("D");
Write JavaScript code using setInterval that increments a counter every second and clears the interval once it reaches 5.
Write JavaScript code that replaces setInterval with a self-rescheduling setTimeout so a slow task never overlaps itself.
Explain and write JavaScript code showing microtask versus macrotask ordering: log inside setTimeout, queueMicrotask, and Promise.then, in expected order.
Write JavaScript code that sets a timeout with an id, cancels it before it fires, and demonstrates clearTimeout with a flag.
Write JavaScript code that demonstrates setTimeout(..., 0) still runs after the current synchronous code and after all pending microtasks.
Write JavaScript code that schedules a chain of nested setTimeouts printing 1, 2, 3 one second apart without using setInterval.
Write JavaScript code that uses queueMicrotask to run a callback after the current function completes but before timers.
Write Node.js code demonstrating process.nextTick versus Promise microtask ordering.
Write JavaScript code for a timer that tracks remaining time so it can be paused and resumed.
Write JavaScript code that batches DOM-less updates with setTimeout(fn, 0) so 1000 rapid calls coalesce into a single flush.
Write JavaScript code that measures how long a synchronous block takes using Date.now before/after and compares it with a setTimeout scheduling delay.
Write JavaScript code that runs three setTimeouts with delays 300, 100, 200 and logs the actual completion order.
Write JavaScript code showing that an uncaught error inside a setTimeout callback cannot be caught by a surrounding try/catch, and how to handle it inside the callback.
Write JavaScript code that implements debounceTimed(fn, wait) using timers, so the trailing call fires only after wait ms of quiet.
Write Node.js code that uses setImmediate to run a callback after I/O events, contrasting it with setTimeout(fn, 0).
Write JavaScript code that creates an interval clock printing the current time every second, returning a stop function.
Write JavaScript code demonstrating that Promise.then callbacks always run before a queued setTimeout(fn, 0) callback.
Write JavaScript code that recursively schedules work with setTimeout and stops when a predicate becomes true.
Write JavaScript code that demonstrates starvation risk: a long synchronous loop blocks a scheduled timer from firing on time.
